hooks.prompt:
A `git push` command just ran in this repo. Hook input JSON (includes tool_input.command and tool_response): $ARGUMENTS

First check tool_response: if the push failed (non-zero exit / error output), do nothing and output no systemMessage.

If it succeeded: run `git log --oneline -10` and `git show --stat HEAD` (and diff earlier commits too if multiple were pushed) to see what was actually pushed. Skim CLAUDE.md at the repo root for project context (this is a TFG/thesis backend project; the student keeps design notes in Obsidian).

Decide if anything in these commits is worth capturing as an Obsidian note — e.g. an architectural or design decision, a non-obvious tradeoff or rationale, an ADR-worthy choice, a roadmap/milestone change, or a gotcha worth remembering later. Routine code changes, formatting, dependency bumps, or small fixes are NOT worth flagging.

If something qualifies: output a systemMessage that names the specific commit(s) and concretely states what to note in Obsidian and why. Keep it short (2-4 sentences).

If nothing qualifies: output no systemMessage at all — stay silent.
hooks.statusMessage: Checking if this push is worth an Obsidian note...
